clue.text: Russell's tree by Cornish river is partly knotty

parts.note: the Tamar forms most of the border between Cornwall and Devon

indicators.note: only part of the word knotty is used here, namely its opening letter

explanation.surface: A tree growing beside a river in Cornwall turns out to be somewhat gnarled.
explanation.walkthrough: Dora Russell called her autobiography The Tamarisk Tree, so 'Russell's tree' is a literary definition.
explanation.definitionFit: Dora Russell's memoir is titled after this feathery shrub, which is the tree she names.

clue.text: Short story in a five-line rhyme scheme describing an Arabianhost

indicators.note: to describe is to draw round, so the rhyme scheme encloses the shortened story

parts.note: ABABA is a pattern of rhymes for a five-line stanza

indicators.note: short means the word for story loses its final letter

parts.note: a lie is a made-up story

explanation.surface: A brief tale set in limerick-like verse portrays a host from Arabia.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Short' drops the last letter of the story word, and 'describing' means drawing a line round. The clue prints 'Arabianhost' run together.
explanation.definitionFit: The Arabian Nights hero hosts the forty thieves' treasure cave, so he is an Arabian host of a kind.

clue.text: Hallucinogen led aunts distractedly to ingest a gram

indicators.note: to ingest is to take in, so the jumbled letters swallow the next piece
acting distractedly suggests confusion, so the letters of led aunts are jumbled

parts.note: g is the standard abbreviation for gram

explanation.surface: A drug sends some aunts into confusion after they swallow a small dose.
explanation.walkthrough: 'distractedly' signals the jumble and 'to ingest' the swallowing; 'a gram' is the usual abbreviation for the unit.
explanation.definitionFit: Angel dust is street slang for PCP, a drug causing hallucinations.

clue.text: Making peace with Mrs Forsyte endlessly in charge

indicators.note: endlessly means the name loses its final letter

parts.note: Irene is the wife of Soames Forsyte in Galsworthy's Forsyte Saga

explanation.surface: Someone reconciles with Galsworthy's heroine while running the show.
explanation.definitionFit: An irenic attitude aims at conciliation, the work of a peacemaker; the word comes from Greek eirene.

clue.text: Lewis's title depicting racism in monarch's noble descent

parts.note: a king is a monarch, here with the possessive
blood means lineage or descent
royal here means of noble rank

explanation.surface: A novelist's book shows prejudice within a family of royal lineage.
explanation.walkthrough: Kingsblood Royal (1947) is Sinclair Lewis's novel about racial prejudice. The pieces come in the order monarch's, descent, noble.
explanation.definitionFit: Sinclair Lewis's 1947 novel about a man discovering black ancestry bears this title.

clue.text: Identification of a new edition of Sapper

indicators.note: a new edition reworks a text, so the letters of the word are reset in fresh order

explanation.surface: A reissue of a Bulldog Drummond author is how one is identified.
explanation.walkthrough: Sapper was the pen name of H. C. McNeile, creator of Bulldog Drummond.
explanation.definitionFit: Papers are documents carried as proof of identity, as in 'show me your papers'.

clue.text: Choose Scots town for clubbable chap

parts.note: to pick is to choose
Wick is a town in Caithness, in the far north of Scotland

explanation.surface: Selecting a Scottish town for a sociable fellow.
explanation.walkthrough: Mr Pickwick founded the Pickwick Club in Dickens's Pickwick Papers.
explanation.definitionFit: Samuel Pickwick heads the club in Dickens's novel, a genial member who loves company.

clue.text: "A thick bonnet, of the same materials, with -s attached to it" (Peveril of the Peak)

definitions.text: "A thick bonnet, of the same materials, with -s attached to it" (Peveril of the Peak)

parts.words: "A thick bonnet, of the same materials, with -s attached to it" (Peveril of the Peak)
parts.note: a quotation from Scott's novel with the missing word to be supplied: a flap on a cap covering the ear

explanation.surface: A quotation from Scott describing a headdress with a missing word.
explanation.definitionFit: Flaps hanging from a bonnet to cover the ears are what Scott's sentence lacks.

clue.text: Salts seas treat roughly?

indicators.note: roughly suggests rough handling, so the letters of seas treat are shaken up

explanation.surface: A question whether seawater treats one harshly, with salts in mind.
explanation.definitionFit: Stearates are chemical salts of stearic acid, used in soaps.

clue.text: Con artist giving brief enjoyment to judge that's popular

parts.note: in means fashionable or popular

indicators.note: brief means the word is cut short, losing its final letter

parts.note: glee is joyful enjoyment

explanation.surface: A swindler offers a judge a short-lived pleasure that goes down well.
explanation.walkthrough: 'brief' cuts GLEE to GLE. Alfred Jingle is the strolling con man of The Pickwick Papers.
explanation.definitionFit: Dickens's Jingle is a fast-talking swindler who tricks the Pickwickians.

clue.text: Swiped a vase we hear, that's depicted in a style of painting by Whistler

definitions.text: a style of painting by Whistler

indicators.note: we hear means the phrase is spoken and its sound gives the answer

parts.note: swiped means knocked, and a vase is an urn, together said as one word

explanation.surface: Someone struck a pot, it is said, one shown in a Whistler picture.
explanation.walkthrough: Whistler titled many moonlit pictures Nocturnes, such as Nocturne in Black and Gold.
explanation.definitionFit: Whistler borrowed a musical term for night pieces to name his dim river paintings.

clue.text: Do I half back TLS perhaps, and some other newspapers?

indicators.note: perhaps suggests something tentative, so these letters are rearranged into another form
half of the word back is taken, its opening two letters

explanation.surface: A writer wonders whether to support the Times Literary Supplement and other papers.
explanation.walkthrough: 'half' takes BA from 'back'; 'perhaps' rearranges DOI + BA + TLS.
explanation.definitionFit: Tabloids are popular newspapers, very different from a literary weekly.

clue.text: Sam, healthier than his master it seems

definitions.meaning: Mr Pickwick's cockney servant in Dickens

definitions.text: healthier than his master it seems
definitions.meaning: more well, comparing his health with his employer's

explanation.definitionFit: Dickens's Sam Weller serves Pickwick, and the surname read as a comparative means in better health.

clue.text: Gun toting Greek character showing the full range of emotions

indicators.note: a gun-toter carries it about, so the gun holds the letter

parts.note: gat is slang for a pistol
mu is a letter of the Greek alphabet

explanation.surface: An armed Greek shows every possible feeling.
explanation.definitionFit: A gamut is a complete scale or range, as in 'the whole gamut of emotions'.

clue.text: Abandoned woman paired with a brigadier by Cheever

definitions.meaning: a wife left alone while her husband plays on the links

definitions.text: paired with a brigadier by Cheever
definitions.meaning: John Cheever's story The Brigadier and the ... pairs the two

explanation.definitionFit: The term names a neglected spouse of a keen golfer and appears in a Cheever title.

clue.text: Where an accident may occur on the snooker table?

definitions.meaning: a stretch of road with many crashes
the spot on which the black ball is placed

explanation.definitionFit: A dangerous road spot and the marked point for the black ball share the name.

clue.text: Fellows come up with Mary Jane for clubbable chap

indicators.note: come up in a down clue means the word is read from bottom to top

parts.note: dons are college fellows
Mary Jane and grass are both slang for cannabis

explanation.surface: College fellows arrive with some cannabis for a sociable friend.
explanation.walkthrough: Augustus Snodgrass is the poetic member of the Pickwick Club; the grid prints the name with G for D.
explanation.definitionFit: Snodgrass is one of Pickwick's fellow club members, all sociable types.

clue.text: Act pleasantly, without a sign of hesitation, to Egaeus's cousin

indicators.note: without in its old sense of outside, so the phrase goes round the hesitation

parts.note: to be nice is to behave pleasantly
er is the sound of someone hesitating, which the grid needs written the other way round

explanation.surface: Someone behaves agreeably, never faltering, towards a relative in a Poe tale.
explanation.walkthrough: The usual hesitation sound is written the other way round, so the setter appears to have slipped. The cousin comes from Poe's story of that name, narrated by Egaeus.
explanation.definitionFit: In Poe's tale the narrator Egaeus is obsessed with his cousin, whose name titles the story.

clue.text: Lightweight narrator of Swallow Barn?

definitions.meaning: a ..., a ton being a weight
Mark ... tells John Pendleton Kennedy's novel Swallow Barn

explanation.definitionFit: Kennedy's narrator Mark Littleton has a name that splits into little plus a heavy weight.

clue.text: A port with a sharper taste than others

definitions.meaning: a Moroccan harbour on the Strait of Gibraltar

definitions.text: with a sharper taste than others
definitions.meaning: more tangy, the comparative of tangy

explanation.definitionFit: The Moroccan seaport and the comparative of tangy are spelt alike.

clue.text: Verses seen in hand-written version of 16 for instance

parts.note: the story at 16 down is by Edgar Allan Poe
MS is the abbreviation for manuscript

explanation.surface: Poetry found in a manuscript of a tale, as an example.
explanation.definitionFit: Poems are compositions in verse.

clue.text: A cause of jealousy and envy, big time

definitions.text: A cause of jealousy and envy

parts.note: mega is slang for huge
an era is a period of time

explanation.surface: Something enormous made people resentful and envious for ages.
explanation.walkthrough: Megaera is one of the three Furies of Greek myth, associated with jealousy.
explanation.definitionFit: The Fury Megaera personifies grudging jealousy in Greek myth.

clue.text: God knows, something happened to this author

definitions.text: God knows, something happened to this author

parts.words: God knows, something happened to this author
parts.note: God Knows and Something Happened are two novels by the author of Catch-22

explanation.surface: Heaven knows what befell a writer.
explanation.definitionFit: Joseph Heller wrote both God Knows and Something Happened.

clue.text: What a star will do topless with a clubbable chap

indicators.note: topless means the word loses its first letter

parts.note: stars twinkle

explanation.surface: A star shines without its top, alongside a sociable fellow.
explanation.walkthrough: Nathaniel Winkle is the would-be sportsman of the Pickwick Club.
explanation.definitionFit: Winkle is one of Pickwick's companions in the club.

clue.text: Employ again to trim the first part of a Rumer Godden novel

indicators.note: trimming cuts off an edge, here the opening letter

parts.words: the first part of a Rumer Godden novel
parts.note: Greengage is the opening word of Godden's The Greengage Summer

explanation.surface: Someone is rehired to edit the opening of a novel.
explanation.definitionFit: To re-engage someone is to hire them again.

clue.text: "… baked in this pie, / Whereof their mother — hath fed" (Titus Andronicus)

definitions.text: "… baked in this pie, / Whereof their mother — hath fed" (Titus Andronicus)

parts.words: "… baked in this pie, / Whereof their mother — hath fed" (Titus Andronicus)
parts.note: Titus tells Tamora she has eaten her sons in a pie, with an adverb about her delicate eating missing

explanation.surface: A gruesome Shakespeare quotation with a missing word.
explanation.definitionFit: Shakespeare's line says Tamora fed delicately, with refined manners, on her sons.

clue.text: By lake and fenland river important discoveries were made by this archaeologist

definitions.text: important discoveries were made by this archaeologist

parts.note: ea is a Fens dialect word for a river or drainage channel
key means crucial or important

explanation.surface: Finds near a lake and a river in the Fens made an archaeologist famous.
explanation.walkthrough: 'important' does double duty on purpose: it gives the final piece while also reading into the definition's description of the finds.
explanation.definitionFit: Louis and Mary Leakey made major fossil finds of early humans in East Africa.

clue.text: Emily, for instance, backing the Spanish lottery

indicators.note: backing means going backwards, so the whole phrase is read in reverse

parts.note: el is the Spanish for the
a draw is a lottery

explanation.surface: Emily supports the Spanish lottery.
explanation.walkthrough: 'backing' reverses the whole phrase, not one piece. Emily Wardle is a daughter of Mr Wardle in The Pickwick Papers.
explanation.definitionFit: Emily is one of the Wardle family, Pickwick's hosts at Dingley Dell.

clue.text: Best time of the week to go to the cricket?

definitions.text: Best time of the week to go to the cricket?

parts.words: Best time of the week to go to the cricket?
parts.note: Sunday as the Christian sabbath, punning on the London cricket ground

explanation.surface: When best to watch a cricket match?
explanation.walkthrough: Lord's is the famous cricket ground in London.
explanation.definitionFit: Sunday is the sabbath named for the Lord, and Lord's is a cricket ground.
